notes: Qujialing culture of the middle Yangtze; the lead and infobox give '3400-2500 BC'; the page notes that 'earlier evidence (3400-3000 BC) may belong to the final phase of the Daxi culture'. Extent: 'centered primarily on the middle Yangtze River region in Hubei and Hunan', 'Most sites are located north of the Yangtze between modern Yichang and Wuhan', type site in 'Jingshan County, Hubei' on the Jianghan Plain, 'bordered by the Dabie Mountains to the west, Dongting Lake to the north' (the page's compass is reversed), and it 'reached southern Shaanxi, northern Jiangxi, and southwest Henan'. The shape is Hubei (without the Daxi's Yichang disc until 3300) + Dongting Lake + Yueyang 80 km (north Hunan), confidence 2. Southwest Henan and southern Shaanxi are not drawn: the Yangshao shape holds Henan, and the page's 'reached' reads as influence. Settlements 'some reaching 263 ha'; the Qujialing site 'a central urban area of 70 ha enclosed by a moat'. Predecessor: the Daxi (infobox); the Yichang disc is gained in 3300 when the Daxi ends. Successor: infobox 'Followed by: Shijiahe culture' (undated on the page, no dossier). 'By 2000 BC, fortifications were no longer maintained' and the Qujialing 'population declined gradually' unlike the Liangzhu; not drawn. No area figure.
